translationRepairs: The Wu king said: 'Because of your words, I too had my doubts.'
The Wu king said: 'Without your words, I too would have suspected him.'

In 微子之言，吾亦疑之, classical 微 means ‘if it were not for / without,’ not ‘because of’; the before inverts that conditional, while the proposed after correctly renders the counterfactual and 疑之 as suspicion of the person just denounced.
Shang having been captured, the envoy captured Wu Zixu.
Shang having been captured, the envoy then tried to capture Wu Zixu.
使者捕伍胥 names the envoy’s attempt to seize Wu Zixu; s0040 shows 使者不敢進 and Wu Zixu’s escape, so a completed ‘captured’ is false and ‘tried to capture’ matches the Chinese sequence.
Chu feared Wu again greatly come, then left Ying, moved to Jiao.
Chu feared Wu again greatly come, then left Ying, moved to Ruo.
徙於鄀 uses the place-name 鄀, read Ruo; English ‘Jiao’ is a wrong reading of that graph, and replacing it with Ruo corrects the toponym without other semantic change.
Wu Zixu having crossed, untied his sword saying: "This sword worth one hundred jin, give to father."
After Wu Zixu had crossed, he unfastened his sword and said, "This sword is worth a hundred in gold; I give it to you, elder."
百金 denotes a value of a hundred in gold, not a weight of one hundred jin; the revision also restores grammatical direct speech.
After Wu Zixu crossed, he unfastened his sword and said: 'This sword is worth one hundred jin. I give it to you, elder.'
After Wu Zixu crossed, he unfastened his sword and said: 'This sword is worth a hundred in gold. I give it to you, elder.'
百金 is a monetary value, not one hundred jin; replacing the false unit corrects the offer without otherwise altering the sentence.
Father said: "Chu law, one who gets Wu Zixu granted five myriads shi grain, rank holding jade gui, how just one hundred jin sword!"

The elder said, "Under Chu law, whoever captures Wu Zixu is granted fifty thousand shi of grain and the rank of Holder of the Jade Tablet. Why would I care for a sword worth merely a hundred in gold?"
The draft again mistakes 百金 for one hundred jin and is not grammatical English; the revision preserves the reward, rank, and fisherman's rhetorical contrast.
The fisherman said: 'Under Chu law, whoever captures Wu Zixu receives fifty thousand shi of grain and the rank of Holder of the Jade Tablet. Why would I care only for a sword worth one hundred jin?'

The fisherman said: 'Under Chu law, whoever captures Wu Zixu receives fifty thousand shi of grain and the rank of Holder of the Jade Tablet. Why would I care for a sword worth merely a hundred in gold?'
百金 is a monetary value rather than a weight of one hundred jin; the revised question restores the intended contrast.
Helü established, achieved ambitions, summoned Wu Yuan envoy, with him planned state affairs.
Once Helü had taken the throne and achieved his ambition, he summoned Wu Yun to serve as envoy and planned affairs of state with him.
The personal name 員 in 伍員 is read Yún; the revision also makes the literal field grammatical while preserving the appointment and consultation.
Once Helü had taken the throne and achieved his ambition, he summoned Wu Yuan to serve as envoy and planned state affairs with him.
Once Helü had taken the throne and achieved his ambition, he summoned Wu Yun to serve as envoy and planned affairs of state with him.
The personal name 員 in 伍員 is read Yún, not Yuán; Wu Yun is the correct romanization of Wu Zixu's personal name.
Wu Zixu said: 'Convey my thanks to Shen Baoxu and say: My sun is setting and the road is long, so I am therefore walking inverted and applying things in reverse.'
Wu Zixu said: 'Offer my apologies to Shen Baoxu and tell him: The sun is setting and the road is long, so I must walk backward and act against the usual order.'
為我謝申包胥 asks the messenger to apologize or explain on Zixu's behalf, not to convey thanks; the revision also gives the proverb idiomatic English.
Wu Zixu said: 'Convey my thanks to Shen Baoxu and tell him: The sun is setting, and the road is long, so I must walk backward and act against the usual order.'
Wu Zixu said: 'Offer my apologies to Shen Baoxu and tell him: The sun is setting, and the road is long, so I must walk backward and act against the usual order.'
謝 here means to apologize or explain through the messenger; 'thanks' reverses the force of Wu Zixu's reply to his old friend.
He became increasingly estranged from Zixu's counsel.
益疏子胥之謀 says the king grew increasingly distant from Zixu's counsel; the draft is ungrammatical and leaves both subject and relation obscure.
He increasingly estranged Wu Zixu's strategies.
He became increasingly estranged from Zixu's counsel.
The draft is ungrammatical and makes 'strategies' the object of an active verb; 疏 marks the king's growing alienation from Zixu's counsel.
Wu Zixu, about to depart, told his son: 'I have repeatedly remonstrated with the king, but the king did not use my advice. I now see Wu's perishing.
As he was about to depart, Wu Zixu told his son: 'I have repeatedly remonstrated with the king, but he has rejected my advice. I can now see that Wu will perish.
The draft's 'see Wu's perishing' is unidiomatic; the revision preserves the prediction and improves the repeated reference to the king.
Wu grand steward Pi already with Wu Zixu had enmity, because slandered: "Wu Zixu character firm violent, little kindness, suspicious treacherous, his resentment fear become deep calamity.

The Grand Steward Pi of Wu already had a grievance against Zixu and therefore slandered him: "Zixu is harsh and violent, shows little kindness, and is suspicious and malicious. I fear his resentment will become a grave calamity.
The draft is ungrammatical and mistranslates 恐 as though Zixu's resentment itself feared something; Pi is saying that he fears the resentment will become a grave danger.

Wu's Grand Steward Pi, already having enmity with Wu Zixu, therefore slandered: 'Wu Zixu in character is firm and violent, with little kindness, suspicious and treacherous. His resentment fears becoming a deep calamity.

The Grand Steward Pi of Wu already had a grievance against Zixu and therefore slandered him: 'Zixu is harsh and violent, shows little kindness, and is suspicious and malicious. I fear his resentment will become a grave calamity.
The draft assigns fear to the resentment and produces nonsensical English; 恐 introduces Pi's warning about the danger he claims Zixu poses.
Former day king wished attack Qi, Wu Zixu considered not can, king finally attacked had great merit.
Previously, when the king wished to attack Qi, Zixu said it should not be done; the king ultimately attacked and won a great victory.
以為不可 means Zixu judged the campaign inadvisable, not that he thought it impossible; the revision also restores grammatical English.
Previously the king wished to attack Qi. Wu Zixu considered it not possible, but the king finally attacked and had great merit.
Previously, when the king wished to attack Qi, Zixu said it should not be done; the king ultimately attacked and won a great victory.
The draft's 'considered it not possible' is awkward and misstates the remonstrance; 不可 here means the campaign should not be undertaken.
Wu Zixu ashamed his plan strategy not used, then reversed resented.
Zixu was ashamed that his counsel had not been accepted and therefore became resentful.
乃反怨望 means that, according to Pi's accusation, Zixu consequently turned resentful; 'reversed resented' is not meaningful English.
Wu Zixu, ashamed that his plans and strategies were not used, then reversed and resented.
Zixu was ashamed that his counsel had not been accepted and therefore became resentful.
The draft mechanically renders 反 and is ungrammatical; the sentence describes Pi's allegation that Zixu turned resentful.
When Wu Zixu distressed on Jiang above, path begged food, ambition how once moment forgot Ying?
When Zixu was in distress beside the Jiang, begging for food along the road, could he have forgotten his resolve to reach Ying for even a moment?
The draft is ungrammatical; 志豈嘗須臾忘郢 asks whether Zixu's purpose of reaching Ying ever left his mind.
When Wu Zixu was trapped on the Jiang and begging for food along the road, could his purpose have forgotten Ying for even a moment?
When Zixu was in distress beside the Jiang, begging for food along the road, could he have forgotten his resolve to reach Ying for even a moment?
The draft incorrectly gives 'purpose' the act of forgetting; the rhetorical question concerns whether Zixu himself ever forgot his objective.
